idiom_name: errgroup.Group (Go/SetLimit/Wait) + context.WithTimeout, results into an index-keyed slice
implementation_notes: errgroup.WithContext is the idiomatic fan-out: g.Go starts one goroutine per recipient, and the derived context is cancelled the first time a function returns a non-nil error - which the still-running recipients observe through ctx.Done(). The deadline is context.WithTimeout derived from the caller's context, errgroup.SetLimit bounds the fan-out width, and replies are gathered without locks into a pre-sized slice indexed by recipient. The Aggregator is ordinary code after g.Wait(); nothing in the language replaces the structure, but the standard library primitives plus this small helper make it a few lines.
code_sketch:
g, ctx := errgroup.WithContext(ctx)
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, budget)
defer cancel()
offers := make([]Offer, len(recipients))
g.SetLimit(8)                              // bound the fan-out width
for i, r := range recipients {
    i, r := i, r
    g.Go(func() error { o, err := ask(ctx, r); offers[i] = o; return err })
}
_ = g.Wait()                               // each slot is zero-valued when its recipient failed
pitfalls: One failing recipient cancels the whole group through the derived context: for a partial gather, do not return errors from g.Go (or use a WaitGroup plus an error channel for the failures you want to keep).
Without SetLimit the fan-out spawns one goroutine and one outbound request per recipient with no bound at all.
Under a pre-1.22 language version the loop variable is shared by all iterations, so the `i, r := i, r` copies are mandatory.
A cancelled call returns an error and a zero value: an empty slot must stay distinguishable from a legitimate empty answer.

variants.name: stdlib-only WaitGroup + reply channel + select deadline
variants.idiom_name: sync.WaitGroup + buffered reply channel + select on timer/ctx.Done()
variants.implementation_notes: The dependency-free form replaces errgroup with channels: every recipient pushes a tagged reply into a buffered channel, and a select loop consumes replies until the expected number arrived, the caller's context is done, or the budget timer fires - the completeness policy is visible in the loop instead of hidden in a helper. Go 1.22 creates loop variables per iteration, so passing the recipient as a parameter is a style choice rather than a correctness requirement. Choose this variant when the gather must tolerate per-recipient failures, when replies should be consumed in completion order, or when x/sync is not available.
pitfalls: A reply channel smaller than the recipient count blocks the losers on send once the gather has returned; size the buffer to the recipient count or drain with a non-blocking select.
time.After allocates a timer that stays armed until it fires; a per-request gather should reuse time.NewTimer and stop it.
Nothing cancels the in-flight calls when the local timer fires: the budget must be pushed into the requests as a context deadline, or the losers keep occupying resources.
